problem: Existing embodied-cognition benchmarks for MLLMs cover only fragmented abilities, rely on simulation or egocentric video with limited realism, and score planning with multiple-choice, BLEU or free-form LLM judging. These metrics miss skill-object dependencies, valid step reorderings and physical feasibility.
motivation: Dual-system robots use an MLLM as System 2 (the 'embodied brain') for reasoning and decision-making, so this component needs systematic evaluation across the whole manipulation pipeline. Open-ended long-horizon plans admit many valid orderings, so a faithful metric must check whether critical object-state milestones are actually reached.
key_idea: RoboBench evaluates MLLMs as embodied brains on 5 dimensions built from real robot data (25 tasks, 6092 QA), and scores long-horizon plans with an MLLM-as-world-simulator that rolls out plans against a human-annotated DAG of milestones.
insight: Text-only GPT-5.4 stays near chance on perception (27.12) and affordance (25.61) versus 67.32 and 85.70 for the best vision model, so the questions require visual grounding. Implicit instructions score much lower than explicit ones (Claude-Sonnet-4.6: 79.94 vs 61.38), and a chain-of-thought rewrite ablation does not reliably close the gap. The simulator judge correlates better with humans (r=0.83) than the LLM-score baseline (r=0.73), and perception and affordance scores predict VLA success on CALVIN and LIBERO respectively.
method: Five dimensions: Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction and Failure Analysis, following the execution pipeline; 14 capabilities, 25 tasks.

Data construction: real robot data (RoboMIND, RH20T, Open-X, AgiBot etc.) plus in-house collection, annotated with Gemini and detection models and refined by humans; multiple-choice QA for perception, affordance and failure, function-template plans for planning.

Q1 long-horizon planning score: (NodeCorrectness + TaskCompletion)/20, where NodeCorrectness is an MLLM one-to-one match on skill/object/parameter and TaskCompletion is the fraction of critical milestones achieved during an MLLM world-simulation rollout from the first frame, the reference actions and the DAG.
Q2 next-step planning (skill exact match plus object and parameter reasonableness) and Q3 task-state estimation (binary accuracy).

Failure data: real VLA rollout failures from RoboMIND labeled by experts for execution errors; REFLECT-style perturbed plans (wrong object, missing step, wrong order, wrong condition) for planning errors.
Quality control: human cross-pass on every MLLM annotation, residual disagreement below 4%, and removal of items all models solve (items all models fail are manually reviewed).
VLA correlation study: 8 VLMs converted to VLAs via minimal fine-tuning (VLM4VLA-style) and evaluated on CALVIN and LIBERO-10, then Pearson-correlated with RoboBench dimension scores.

setting.backbone: Evaluated MLLMs: GPT-5.4/5.2/5/4.1/4o, Claude Opus 4.7/Sonnet 4.6/4.5/Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro/2.5 Pro/2.5 Flash, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LLaVA-OneVision-7B, RoboBrain-2.0-7B, RoboBrain-2.5-4B, MiMo-Embodied-7B (all evaluated zero-shot); LLM judges for planning
setting.training_data: none (benchmark paper; models evaluated zero-shot; VLA correlation study uses minimal fine-tuning of small VLMs)
setting.observation: Real robot images, multi-view images and videos/frames (first frame for Q1, ~10 frames for Q2 and Q3)
setting.action_space: Function-template skill sequences such as pick_up(object) and move_to(object, target), plus multiple-choice points, trajectories and base positions
setting.simulator: none for the benchmark (real robot data); CALVIN and LIBERO simulators for the VLA correlation study
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT DAG and reference plan are used only by the evaluator judge)

numbers_note: Benchmark paper: results are MLLM scores on RoboBench's own tasks (not a canonical navigation benchmark), so no entries are extracted.
results: Gemini-3.1-Pro leads perception (67.32 avg), affordance (85.70 avg) and failure analysis (52.95 avg), while Claude-Sonnet-4.6 leads planning (Q1 avg 79.38) and instruction comprehension (70.66). Closed-source models beat open-source by about 20 points on average. Weaknesses include implicit instructions, robot-view and temporal grounding (best scores 53.62 and 50.38) and execution-error diagnosis (best 43.71).
limitations: Q1 planning scores depend on an MLLM judge, which is only approximately human-aligned (r=0.83), and the VLA correlation study covers only 8 VLMs with several correlations not significant.
Focuses on manipulation-centric high-level cognition from offline QA, so it does not measure closed-loop execution or navigation performance.
